hunt.justification: AWS Console access is the primary control plane for cloud resources; a successful takeover can lead to full organizational compromise. Triaging this chain centrally ensures uniform response for decentralized teams.

meta.name: AWS Cloud Identity Takeover Chain

related.reason: This hunt focuses on the takeover chain behavior, while the alternative would focus directly on the IAM management events if they were ingested.

meta.analysis: A single rule can detect a brute force; this hunt correlates that brute force with password resets and successful logons to different accounts across 100 projects, then follows the session to identify post-compromise network activity—a cross-surface correlation no single rule can perform.

coverage.reason: Requires management-plane events like PutUserPolicy which are not visible in the provided normalized surfaces.
Requires management-plane visibility into access key lifecycle events.

scenario.summary: The campaign involves an AWS account takeover sequence beginning with credential-stuffing or brute-force attempts on the AWS Management Console. Once an account is compromised, the actor performs a password reset, escalates privileges within the cloud environment, and generates long-term persistence through the creation of new AWS access keys.

meta.rationale: Scope to the central origin project. The initial queries cover all linked projects by default; use the scope_hosts parameter to isolate specific AWS accounts identified as targets. Known admin IPs are excluded to focus on user-driven activity.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has gained initial access to a cloud account by brute-forcing the console and performing a password reset, then used that access to establish a presence across multiple projects in the organization.

admin_ips.description: Known administrative or automation IPs to exclude from scoping counts.

scope_hosts.description: The AWS Account IDs (dst_endpoint_name) to focus on; leave empty to hunt across all 100 linked projects.

lookback_days.description: Days of history to examine for brute force and follow-on activity.

suspicious_ips.description: IPs identified in the first agent read to pivot on in the follow-on stage.

reset_indicators.description: Specific activity_name values in authentication logs that indicate account modification.

failed_logon_threshold.description: Number of failed attempts from a single IP before it is considered a brute-force lead.

hunt.name: AWS Cloud Identity Takeover Chain
hunt.description: This hunt triages AWS identity takeover attempts across a centralized SOC managing 100 projects. It starts by identifying brute-force patterns and password-reset markers on the authentication surface, then pivots to successful logons and subsequent network traffic to confirm the transition from attempt to takeover. By acting centrally on a single origin but validating across linked projects, analysts can contain compromised cloud identities across the entire organization.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name AS aws_account, COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{admin_ips}}' = '' OR NOT (instr(',' || '{{admin_ips}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0)) GROUP BY dst_endpoint_name
config.description: Find every AWS account recording activity to scope the hunt across the organization projects while excluding administrative noise.
config.expected_signal: A list of AWS account names and their event volume excluding known admin IPs. Silence means no AWS authentication events were recorded.

primitive_config.label: Inventory AWS Accounts
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name AS aws_account, COUNT(*) AS event_count FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{admin_ips}}' = '' OR NOT (instr(',' || '{{admin_ips}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0)) GROUP BY dst_endpoint_name
primitive_config.expected: A list of AWS account names and their event volume excluding known admin IPs. Silence means no AWS authentication events were recorded.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS targeted_users, COUNT(*) AS failures, MIN(time) AS first_failure, MAX(time) AS last_failure FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND activity_id = 5 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING failures >= {{failed_logon_threshold}} ORDER BY failures DESC
config.description: Identify source IPs targeting one or more users with high failure volumes.
config.expected_signal: Source IPs with failure counts exceeding the threshold. High failure counts across many users indicate a spray; high counts for one user indicate brute force.

primitive_config.label: AWS Console Brute Force
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS targeted_users, COUNT(*) AS failures, MIN(time) AS first_failure, MAX(time) AS last_failure FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND activity_id = 5 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING failures >= {{failed_logon_threshold}} ORDER BY failures DESC
primitive_config.expected: Source IPs with failure counts exceeding the threshold. High failure counts across many users indicate a spray; high counts for one user indicate brute force.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name, dst_endpoint_name, activity_name, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND activity_id = 99 AND instr(',' || '{{reset_indicators}}' || ',', ',' || activity_name || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify management-related authentication activity from the same time window.
config.expected_signal: Authentication metadata events matching the reset keywords. These indicate the persistence stage of the takeover.

primitive_config.label: Suspected Password Modification
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name, dst_endpoint_name, activity_name, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND activity_id = 99 AND instr(',' || '{{reset_indicators}}' || ',', ',' || activity_name || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Authentication metadata events matching the reset keywords. These indicate the persistence stage of the takeover.

config.objective: Identify the source IPs that performed brute-force attempts and then reached a password reset event. Prioritize IPs that appear in both console-brute-force and suspected-password-resets results as they represent the highest risk.
config.description: Determine if the brute-force attempts and modification events originate from the same sources.
config.expected_signal: A list of high-confidence suspicious source IPs that pivot into the follow-on stage.
config.success_criteria: A verdict per IP citing specific rows that show the progression from failure to modification.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) AS account_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) AS accounts, MIN(time) AS first_success, MAX(time) AS last_success FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND activity_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_name || ',') > 0) AND ('{{suspicious_ips}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_ips}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name
config.description: Confirm if the identified IPs successfully logged in to any account and check if they reached multiple distinct accounts.
config.expected_signal: Rows naming a successful logon from a source IP previously seen brute-forcing. Multiple accounts indicate organization-wide compromise.

primitive_config.label: Successful Logons from Suspicious IPs
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) AS account_count, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) AS accounts, MIN(time) AS first_success, MAX(time) AS last_success FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'aws' AND activity_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_name || ',') > 0) AND ('{{suspicious_ips}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_ips}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, actor_user_name
primitive_config.expected: Rows naming a successful logon from a source IP previously seen brute-forcing. Multiple accounts indicate organization-wide compromise.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, protocol, COUNT(*) AS connections FROM hb_network_connection WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{suspicious_ips}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_ips}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, protocol
config.description: Determine if the attacker IPs are interacting with other infrastructure after the logon.
config.expected_signal: Connections from the brute-force IPs to unexpected destinations. This establishes the post-logon behavior.

config.objective: Determine if the evidence supports a continuous chain from brute-force attempt to successful account takeover and operational usage. Factor in the early auth findings and follow-on pivots.
config.description: Synthesize the auth success and network markers to confirm active exploitation of a cloud identity.
config.expected_signal: A final malicious/suspicious/benign verdict per identity.
config.success_criteria: A per-identity verdict citing the transition from failures to success and any subsequent network traffic.

config.question: the confirm-account-takeover verdict is malicious for at least one cloud identity
config.condition: the confirm-account-takeover verdict is malicious for at least one cloud identity
config.description: Direct response actions based on the confirmed takeover status.
Revoke sessions and deactivate credentials to stop the takeover.
config.instructions: Revoke all active IAM sessions and deactivate all existing access keys for the actor_user_name identified in the malicious verdict.

config.description: Analyze management-plane events that are not visible in normalized surfaces to find privilege escalation.
config.instructions: Review the raw CloudTrail logs for the compromised user to find evidence of PutUserPolicy, AttachUserPolicy, or CreateAccessKey events that occurred after the suspicious logon.

config.description: Document findings across the 100 projects and recommend architectural hardening.
config.instructions: Record the full takeover chain; recommend enabling MFA and IP-based conditional access for all console users across all organizational projects.
